extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing, filing, and examining reissue patent applications (including divisional/continuation reissues, restriction/election issues, disclaimers, oath/declaration and assignee consent requirements, and multiple reissue application practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction between original and newly added claims (37 CFR 1.176(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.176(b) permits the examiner to require restriction in a reissue application between claims newly added in a reissue application and the original patent claims, where the added claims are directed to an invention which is separate and distinct from the invention(s) defined by the original patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria for making a restriction requirement in a reissue application between the newly added claims and the original claims are the same as that applied in a non-reissue application (see MPEP §§ 806 through 806.05(i)). The authority extends to making an election of species. For reissue applications of patents issued from a U.S. national stage application submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371, the restriction should not be made under the PCT unity standard because reissue is filed under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive election and examiner actions when restriction required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a restriction requirement is made by the examiner, the original patent claims will be held to be constructively elected (except where a disclaimer of all patent claims is filed in the reissue application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Office action containing the restriction requirement, the examiner should suggest filing a divisional reissue directed to the constructively non-elected invention(s). The Office action should (1) provide notification of the restriction requirement, (2) hold the added claims to be constructively non-elected and withdrawn from consideration, (3) treat the original patent claims on the merits, and (4) inform applicant that if original claims are found allowable and no error (other than failure to present non-elected claims) is being corrected, and a divisional has been filed, further action will be suspended pending resolution of the divisional. Non-elected claims will be held in abeyance and only examined if filed in a divisional reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer of all original patent claims (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a disclaimer of all the original patent claims is filed in the reissue application containing newly added claims that are separate and distinct from the original patent claims, only the newly added claims will be present for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclaimer must be filed before the issuance of the examiner’s Office action treating the original patent claims on the merits. Once the Office action treating original claims on the merits has issued, it is too late to obtain examination on the added claims in the reissue application by filing such a disclaimer; a divisional reissue must be filed. Under 37 CFR 1.176(b) the disclaimer cannot be withdrawn; cancellation of all original patent claims is not an effective alternative to a disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of original claims prior to examination — disclaimer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If all original patent claims are canceled prior to examination and no new claims are directed to invention(s) covered by the original patent claims, the examiner may notify applicant that a disclaimer of the original patent claims is required if examination of the new claims is desired in the present reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may provide a time period for applicant to file the disclaimer. If applicant does not file a disclaimer, the examiner shall deem the canceled original patent claims as elected by original presentation and claims to new independent and distinct inventions will be withdrawn from examination; non-elected claims will only be examined if filed in a divisional reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application containing only original unamended claims — rejection for lack of error (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue application contains only original (unamended) patent claims which are found allowable, a rejection will be made under 35 U.S.C. 251 on the basis that there is no 'error' in the non-amended patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office action making this rejection should advise applicant that a proper response must include: (A) a request to suspend action pending completion of examination of a divisional reissue application directed to constructively non-elected invention(s), (B) filing the divisional reissue application or identifying one already filed (by number), and (C) an argument that a complete response has been made based on filing the divisional and the suspension request. The action should set a three-month period to file the divisional. If no divisional is timely filed, no reissue patent will issue because no error in the original patent is being corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and merger requirement when divisional timely filed (37 CFR 1.177(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a divisional reissue application is timely filed, the divisional will be examined and action in the first reissue application containing the original patent claims will be suspended once those claims are determined allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further suspensions (usually six-month periods) may be granted to await completion of examination in the divisional. Once a divisional containing added claims is determined allowable, the examiner will issue a requirement under 37 CFR 1.177(c) for applicant to merge the claims of the suspended first reissue application with the allowable claims of the divisional into a single application (place all claims in one application and expressly abandon the other). The requirement will set a two-month period for compliance. Failure to timely respond or refusal to comply may result in the divisional passing to issue alone while prosecution reopens in the suspended first reissue application and a rejection based on lack of error under 35 U.S.C. 251 is made (which may be made final). Abandonment of the first reissue can result in surrender of the original patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction among original patent claims prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: As stated in 37 CFR 1.176(b), the examiner is not permitted to require restriction among original claims of the patent (i.e., among claims that were in the patent before filing the reissue application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where the original patent contains claims to different inventions which the examiner considers independent or distinct, and the reissue application claims the same inventions, a restriction requirement would be improper and must be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction among newly added claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction between multiple inventions recited in the newly added claims will be permitted provided the added claims are drawn to several separate and distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such a case the original patent claims would be examined in the first reissue application and applicant may file divisional reissue applications for each separate and distinct invention identified in the examiner’s restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species and rejoin requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an election of species requirement is made between species claimed in the original patent claims and a claimed species added in the reissue application, if (1) the non-elected claims to the added species depend from (or otherwise include all limitations of) a generic claim which embraces all species claims, and (2) the generic claim is found allowable, then the non-elected claims directed to the added species that was not subject to restriction in the original prosecution must be rejoined with the elected claims of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 821.04(a) for rejoin practice and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reissue applications — notice in first sentence (37 CFR 1.177(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files more than one application for the reissue of a single patent, each such application must contain or be amended to contain in the first sentence of the specification a notice stating that more than one reissue application has been filed and identifying each of the reissue applications by relationship, application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may correct by certificate of correction any reissue patent resulting from an application that does not contain the required notice. The examiner should object and require amendment if applicant fails to include the cross-reference in the first sentence. Examples of acceptable language are provided in the MPEP and examiners should require the cross-reference; if an application issues without it, SPE/SPRS should initiate a certificate of correction (form paragraph 10.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of all patent claims in each reissue application (37 CFR 1.177(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one application for reissue is filed, each claim of the patent being reissued must be presented in each of the reissue applications as an amended, unamended, or canceled (shown in brackets) claim, with each such claim bearing the same number as in the patent being reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same claim of the patent being reissued may not be presented in its original unamended form for examination in more than one of such multiple reissue applications. Added claims must be numbered following the highest-numbered original patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when the same claim presented in multiple reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same claim of the patent is presented for examination in more than one of the reissue applications, in different amended versions, certain rejections are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make: (A) a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 that the reissue application is not correcting an error in the original patent because original claim would be superseded by reissuance in the other application; and (B) a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112 that the claim is indefinite because the invention is not particularly pointed out and distinctly claimed due to inconsistent coverage between applications. Applicant should be advised to revise one application and cancel/present appropriately in the other (example procedure provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting considerations in multiple reissue practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same or similar claims are presented in more than one of the multiple reissue applications, the possibility of statutory or nonstatutory double patenting should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate double patenting rejections should be made. A terminal disclaimer may be filed to overcome a nonstatutory double patenting rejection. The terminal disclaimer is necessary to ensure common ownership in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3) or common enforcement in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(d)(3) of the reissue patents during enforcement in the remainder of the original patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of divisional reissue filing by OPAP when parent consent and oath copies provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a divisional reissue application is filed with a copy of the assignee consent and a copy of the oath/declaration from the parent reissue application, OPAP should accept the copy of the assignee consent and the reissue oath/declaration and accord the divisional reissue application a filing date so long as all other filing requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should review the assignee consent and oath/declaration as discussed in subsections on assignee consent and reissue oath/declaration; acceptance for filing does not preclude later rejection on substantive grounds if the documents are improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent — when a copy is acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the assignee consent is only acceptable if the divisional reissue application is correcting an error for which consent was previously made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a divisional reissue application is filed with a copy of the assignee consent from the parent reissue application but with a newly executed reissue oath/declaration, the copy of the assignee consent should not be accepted because submission of a new oath indicates correction of a different error. In such circumstances OPAP will accord a filing date but the examiner should reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require submission of a new assignee consent (see MPEP § 1410.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration copy acceptance conditions (37 CFR 1.175(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for the inventor’s oath or declaration for a continuing reissue application that claims the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) in compliance with § 1.78 may be satisfied by a copy of the inventor’s oath or declaration from the earlier-filed reissue application, provided that: (i) the inventor executed an oath for the earlier-filed reissue application, (ii) the continuing reissue application does not seek to enlarge the scope of the claims of the original patent, or (iii) the application for the original patent was filed under § 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the remarks accompanying a continuing reissue application, applicant should explain why the copy is sufficient. If the copy does not comply with 37 CFR 1.175(f)(1), the examiner should reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being based on a defective oath/declaration and require a new oath/declaration (see MPEP § 1414).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA continuing reissue oath/declaration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.175(e), the filing of any continuing reissue application which does not replace its parent reissue application must include an oath or declaration which identifies at least one error in the original patent not corrected by the parent reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to pre-AIA rules, a copy of the oath/declaration from the earlier reissue may only be used where the continuing reissue application replaces its parent. If a copy from the parent does not comply, the examiner should reject claims and require a new oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must check error statement in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should check the copy of the oath/declaration to ensure that it identifies an error being corrected by the continuing (divisional/continuation) reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For divisional reissue applications, the copy of the oath/declaration from the parent may or may not cover the error being corrected. If it does not cover the error, the examiner should reject the claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being based on a defective oath/declaration and require a new oath/declaration (see MPEP § 1414).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification on filing to avoid Bauman-type (non-reissue) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If filing a continuation reissue application as opposed to a Bauman type continuation application, there must be an identification, on filing, that the application is a continuation reissue application; likewise for a divisional reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application data sheet or specification states the application is a 'continuation' or 'divisional' of its parent reissue application without indicia, it may be treated as a Bauman type continuation (which is not a reissue and cannot claim the original patent filing date). The application data sheet should separately identify the application as (1) a continuation or divisional of the parent reissue application, and (2) a reissue of the original patent. Examples of acceptable first-sentence continuity language are provided in the MPEP (Examples 1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicia that a continuing reissue application is being filed (recommended list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicia that a continuing reissue application is being filed include: (1) a 37 CFR 1.175 reissue oath/declaration (not merely a copy of the parent's), (2) a specification and/or claims in proper double-column reissue format per 37 CFR 1.173, (3) amendments in proper format per 37 CFR 1.173, (4) a 37 CFR 3.73 statement of assignee ownership and consent by assignee, (5) a correct transmittal letter identifying the application as a reissue filing under 35 U.S.C. 251 (Form PTO/AIA/50 recommended), and (6) an identification phrase in the specification such as 'a reissue continuation of application number [parent]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended that the first line of the specification contain the continuity language to help ensure Office recognizes the application as a continuation reissue or divisional reissue application even if the application data sheet contains the benefit claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Correction procedure for missing cross-reference (form ¶10.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the divisional reissue applications of the family has issued without the required cross reference to the other reissue application(s), the SPE or SPRS will initiate a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.322 to include the appropriate cross reference in the already issued first reissue patent before passing the pending reissue application to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 10.19 (Memorandum - Certificate of Correction (Cross-Reference to Other Reissues in Family)) should be used; the examiner should refer the matter to SPE/SPRS, who prepare a memorandum for the Certificates of Correction Branch. The examiner should make a reference in the pending divisional reissue application to the fact that a certificate of correction has been initiated (e.g., entry in search notes or an examiner’s amendment).
